courses.description: Covers the foundations of electromagnetics for engineers. After a brief review of vector calculus and introduction to Maxwell's equations, major topics include electrostatics, magnetostatics, electrodynamics, electromagnetic waves, and transmission lines. The course concludes with an introduction to antennas and radiofrequency safety.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Electrical and Computer Engineering Design Project
courses.description: Working in teams, students will complete an electrical engineering design project that draws on their knowledge and skills obtained in previous courses. Student teams will design a structure, system, or process to meet a broad range of specified constraints. The development process should consider a broad range of constraints including health and safety, sustainable development and environmental stewardship. Students will manage their projects professionally, prepare a comprehensive written report, and present their design work orally.
courses.prereqText: CS 1023 or CS 1083, ECE 3031 and 46 additional credit hours of ECE core courses.

source.section: ECE 4040 Electrical and Computer Engineering Design Project

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Instrumentation Design
courses.description: This course considers the design of a general-purpose data acquisition system. The electronic design engineer of today can no longer be thought of as a digital or analog designer. Consequently, this course melds the analog and digital electronics areas with a unified engineering approach emphasizing the practical aspects involved. Computer aided design tools are used wherever possible.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Electronic Circuit Design (O)
courses.description: Considers the philosophy and practice of the design of semiconductor circuits.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Devices and Circuits for VLSI
courses.description: Introduction to circuit design and layout. Basic digital gates and clocked systems. Basic RF circuits and components and devices for RF. CAD tools for simulation and layout.

source.section: ECE 4173 Devices and Circuits for VLSI

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Computer Architecture
courses.description: Important aspects of computer architecture will be covered with a unifying theme of computer systems performance. Topics include computer evolution, system busses, main memory, cache memory, memory management, CPU structure, CPU pipelining, superscalar processors, reduced instruction set computers, 64-bit compressors, and paralell processing architectures.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Real Time Systems
courses.description: Real time system design and implementation: basic concurrency theory including scheduling, mutual exclusion and process management, task synchronization and communication, operating system kernels, real time system hardware, software for real time embedded systems.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Digital Communications
courses.description: Covers the fundamentals of modern digital communications, coding and information theory, error detection and correction, data compression, modulation and models for telecommunications and current international standards.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Digital Systems Designs
courses.description: Advanced study of the digital system design methodology. Design methods, models and approaches including: RTL Design, SOC design, and testing methodologies, Intellectual Property (IP), reuse, software-hardware co-design, hardware description languages (HDL), structural and behavioral models, design for low power. One or more design projects.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: VLSI Systems Design
courses.description: Methods and tools for the design of FPGA-based digital circuits with focus on large-scale systems, i.e. digital signal and arithmetic processors, microcomputers. VLSI design process, standards, constraints, implementation, technology-dependent optimization, simulation, testing, and verification. Multi-FPGA systems. FGPA-based peripheral devices. One or more design projects.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Modern Control Systems and Applications
courses.description: Introduces the industrial context for the application of control theory, including system modeling (linear, nonlinear, discrete, continuous and probabilistic models) and problem definition, determining system components and architectures, dealing with limitations and constraints (nonlinearity, disturbances and uncertainties), standard and advanced controls design (linear, nonlinear, and optimal control methods) and tuning methods. Computer-aided controls engineering is emphasized (algorithms/MATLAB).
courses.prereqText: ECE 3312 or CHE 4601 or ME 3623, STAT 2593

source.section: ECE 4323 Modern Control Systems and Applications

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Robotics
courses.description: This is a project-based course where students design a variety of subsystems that are integrated and tested on a mobile robot. Topics include: actuators, PWM, H-bridges, position and range sensors, velocity sensors, optical sensors and switches, strain gauges, position and velocity control, electro-mechanical subsystems, planning and trajectory generation, computer software and hardware interfacing.
courses.prereqText: ECE 3221 or equivalent, ECE 3312 or equivalent.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Haptic Robotics
courses.description: Haptics is the science and technology of creating the sensation of touch using robotic devices. This course will cover the three interelated domains of human physiology, mechatronics and control, to develop haptic robots that render a variety of environments.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Software Design Fundamentals
courses.description: Establish a foundation for designing well-structured application using object-oriented programming. Learn about data abstraction, encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, and the principles of reuseable object-oriented design. Also learn how to use modern software development tools for version control, dependency management, and code synthesis (with AI) while building an application. NOTE: May not be taken for credit by BCS or BScSwE students. Credit will only be counted for one of CS 2013, CS 2033, CS 2043, or ECE 4403.

creditRestrictions.text: May not be taken for credit by BCS or BScSwE students.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Safety Critical Design
courses.description: This elective covers the reliability, availability and fault tolerance of computer systems. It introduces topics related to fault-tolerant computing reliability of hardware and software implementation of engineering systems. It includes fail-safe and fail-operate computer systems design, qualitative analysis of safety-critical systems, risk analysis, fault tolerance techniques, reparability, and redundancy.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Communication Systems
courses.description: Introduces analog and digital communication in the presence of noise. Techniques and application of basic information theory.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Digital Signal Processing I
courses.description: Fundamentals of discrete-time processing. Difference equations and their solutions; the Z transform and its properties. Transfer function, frequency response, impulse response, and realization structures for discrete-time systems, cross-correlation, and power spectral density. Discrete time filters: types, effects of pole-zero placement, the Bilinear Transform. Circular convolution and the DFT.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Digital Signal Processing II
courses.description: Fourier Methods, Fast Fourier Transform, Filter design, Windows, State Variable Methods, Estimation.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to Pattern Recognition
courses.description: An introduction to pattern recognition and its applications. Topics include Bayesian decision theory and parameter estimation, feature generation and selection, parametric vs. nonparametric classification techniques, supervised vs. unsupervised, learning and clustering.
courses.prereqText: CS 1003 or CS 1073, and successful completion of 110 ch in the engineering program.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Rotating Field Electric Machines
courses.description: Examines the operation and structure of three-phase induction motors, single-phase induction motors, three-phase synchronous motors, three-phase synchronous permanent magnet motors. IntroducesExplores the operation of AC electric motors in variable frequency drives (VFDs), variable voltage drives (VVDs), and variable frequency and voltage drives (VFVDs). Discovers applications of electric motor drives in electrified transportation systems, electric vehicles, oil and gas sector, and other emerging applications.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Power System Analysis
courses.description: This course starts with the structure and performance of three-phase synchronous generators for power system applications. The basic structures of power systems (the isolated and interconnected power systems) are presented. The modeling of power system components are introduced in this course, along with the per-unit system and single-line diagrams. The matrix modeling with the admittance and impedance matrices are introduced as a practical method for different power system analysis studies. The power flow formulation and solution methods are provided with the help of software tools. The last part of the course is fault analysis, which models power systems under different fault types. It also provides methods used to perform fault analysis, and selection of grounding designs.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Power Electronics
courses.description: This course covers the modeling, structure, features, control, and applications of switching elements for high power converters. In this course, thyristors, diodes, MOSFETs, BJTs, IGBTs are analyzed for their behaviors in different switching circuits, control circuits, and snubber circuits. Power electronic converters are also presented, along with their models, operation, switching schemes, characteristics, and sample applications. The covered power electronic converters are the switch-mode AC-DC, AC-AC, DC-DC, and DC-AC for single and three phase topologies.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Data Communications and Networking
courses.description: Data transmission fundamentals including signal encoding, error control, flow controls, multiplexing, switching. Protocol architectures (OS, TCP/IP, IPv6). Network protocols peer to peer, medium access control, routing. Local area networks: Ethernet, wireless.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: RF Engineering
courses.description: Builds upon the foundations of engineering electromagnetics to prepare students for a career or further study in radiofrequency (RF) engineering. Major topics include time-domain reflectometry, advanced transmission lines, impedance matching, scattering parameters, RF devices, antennas and propagation, and radio receivers and noise. Students are introduced to industry-standard RF test equipment, including signal generators, vector network analyzers, and spectrum analyzers. The laboratory experience concludes with a student-led experiment on a device or topic of their choosing.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Communications and Network Engineering
courses.description: Advanced network architectures: RSVP, MLPS, RTP. Modeling and simulation of data networks: queuing models for media access, error control and traffic management protocols, modeling of traffic and inter-arrival time, performance analysis. Communication network design. Network management and security.
courses.prereqText: STAT 2593 or STAT 3083; ECE 3221 or CS 2545.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Microwave Engineering
courses.description: Topics related to modern microwave systems including design and measurement of passive microwave circuits.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Fundamentals of Photonics
courses.description: Covers theories of light electromagnetic optics, and photon optics, as well as the interaction of light with matter, and the theory of semiconductor materials/devices and their optical properties. Students will be introduced to new paradigms on the generation of light by luniescence sources such as light-emitting diodes, the transmission of light throughoptical components, waveguides, and fibres, with an emphasis on their applications in quantum technology for communications. The gained knowledge will be leveraged to design integrated photonic circuits in group projects. This course strengthens skills in (a) photonic technology, (b) semiconductor devices, and (c) general knowledge about quantum technology.
courses.prereqText: ECE 3111 and ECE 3821, or permission from the instructor.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Millimeter Wave Technologies
courses.description: Introduces principles of millimeter-wave (mmWave) wireless system design and development, emphasizing challenges and opportunities at these frequencies. Covers propagation, antenna/array design, semiconductor devices, circuits, architectures, and industry standards. Trains students to analyze challenges, address design trade-offs, integrate systems, and explore emerging architectures shaping next-generation networks.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Independent Project
courses.description: An independent project. Students work under the supervision of a chosen faculty member. Students are responsible for finding a supervisor and initiating the project. Deliverables include a comprehensive report detailing the work.
courses.prereqText: Successful completion of 110 ch in the engineering program.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to Biomedical Engineering
courses.description: Introduces biomedical concepts in the context of electrical engineering. Topics covered include basic anatomy and physiology, biopotential origination and modelling, biosignal measurement instrumentation, biosignal analysis and a survey of medical devices and health care technologies.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Special Studies in Electrical Engineering
courses.description: With the approval of the Department Chair and under the guidance of a member of the faculty, a student may perform special studies and investigations related to the undergraduate program. Restricted to students in their final year of study.

source.section: ECE 4933 Special Studies in Electrical Engineering

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Topics in Computer Engineering
courses.description: A selected area of computer engineering with a unifying theme will be explored in depth. The topics covered are selected from one or more of the following areas: parallel processing, operating systems, concurrent system performance, network based parallel computing, embedded system issues, algorithms in real-time, computer system modeling analysis.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Principles of Microeconomics
courses.description: Study economic choices and how they are impacted by incentives and government intervention. Economics breaks into micro and macro halves. Microeconomics focuses on individuals, firms, products, and pricing. Explore how prices and wages are determined, the effects of taxation, price ceilings/floors, and quotas. Understand key concepts for analyzing behavior and public policy effects. NOTE: Credit cannot be counted for both ECON 1013 and ECON 1014 or ECON 1073.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Principles of Microeconomics: Critical Perspectives
courses.description: This course is an alternative introduction to microeconomics. The aim is to be less comprehensive than ECON 1013, but to go deeper into the core topics to provide a more thorough critical perspective. In the process, the political and philosophical ideas underlying conventional economic conclusions are examined. The limitations of conventional economic reasoning, and the biases that may exist, are exposed. NOTE: Students with credit in ECON 1013 or ECON 1073 may not take this course for credit.

source.section: ECON 1014 Principles of Microeconomics: Critical Perspectives

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Principles of Macroeconomics
courses.description: Study macroeconomics to understand the determinants of employment, unemployment, inflation, and growth. Understand the building blocks of the neoclassical model to explain interest rates, exchange rates, and how the government can help to stabilize the economy. Gain insight into wealth disparities among countries. NOTE: Credit cannot be counted for both ECON 1023, and ECON 1024 or ECON 1073.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Principles of Macroeconomics: Critical Perspectives
courses.description: This course is an alternative introduction to macroeconomics. As in ECON 1023, the standard 'neoclassical' model is presented and explained. While this model has long been criticized by heterodox economists - those in other schools of thought than the neoclassical school - there was, until recently, a consensus within the neoclassical school itself. The 2007 financial meltdown, and the subsequent Great Recession, has changed that. This course exposes students to the ongoing debates, their historical roots, and their political implications. NOTE: Students with credit in ECON 1023 or ECON 1073 may not take this course for credit.

source.section: ECON 1024 Principles of Macroeconomics: Critical Perspectives

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Economics for Engineers
courses.description: Explore core economic principles crucial for engineering and computer science. This course covers price, production, and cost theory. , It then examines aggregate supply and demand. It also delves into money, banking, public finance, and international economics. This knowledge will equip students to understand economic factors that influence their technical fields and future careers. NOTE: Registration restricted to students in an Engineering or Computer Science degree program. Credit cannot be counted for both ECON 1073 and another first-year ECON course.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: The Chinese Economy in Transition (O)
courses.description: This course surveys the working of the contemporary Chinese economy in its various aspects. Topics to be covered include the background to China's economic reform and its process, China's economic transition, factors contributing to China's fast economic growth, economic institutions, economic policy, and economic issues in contemporary China.

source.section: ECON 2008 The Chinese Economy in Transition (O)

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Understanding Economics through Film (O)
courses.description: This course develops a vocabulary and a set of tools to analyse films, and utilizes the motion picture to establish the context for teaching economics concepts. Plots and subplots of selected films are used to illustrate problems and issues that are amenable to economic analysis. Through a combination of readings, lectures, discussion and films, students will develop a set of skills characterized as an economic way of thinking. The course is designed for undergraduates with no previous economic training.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Introduction to Economic Governance
courses.description: This course introduces students to the role and functions of the public sector in the economic system. Topics include the rationale for government activities, the emergence of public/private collaborative initiatives, the impact of specific government programs, overall fiscal policy and government stabilization programs, policies designed to stimulate economic growth, and policies designed to protect the environment. These policies are considered in the context of intergovernmental fiscal relations and the inherent potential for conflict between different levels of government.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Feminist Perspectives in Economics
courses.description: Examine the critiques of basic neoclassical microeconomic theory from a gender economics perspective. Learn the history of feminist economics. In addition, learn the history of economics through the women working in the field of economics and the challenges they faced throughout their careers.
courses.prereqText: Any first-year (1000-level) microeconomics course or permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Intermediate Microeconomics
courses.description: Microeconomics has two main purposes. First, it is a foundation course in the study of economics; it provides the essential building blocks for higher level economics and finance courses. Second, microeconomics can be directly applied to help solve the day-to-day decisions of business managers; issues such as pricing, production, advertising, and strategic interaction. It achieves this through extensive use of real-world examples and short case studies.
courses.prereqText: 3 ch of first-year microeconomics (ECON 1013, or, ECON 1014), or ECON 1073.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: The Economics of Strategic Thinking
courses.description: Strategic thinking is the art of outdoing an adversary, knowing that the adversary is trying to do the same to you. All of us must practice strategic thinking at work as well as in everyday life. As a business manager, political adviser, lawyer and in the day-to-day pursuits of life (such as buying a car) you will be trying to win the competition. This unit is about the basic principles students can adopt in the attempt to become a better competitive strategist in business and daily life. The unit draws these principles from the fields of business, politics, law, sports, warfare, fiction and modern art forms such as the movies.
courses.prereqText: First-year microeconomics (ECON 1013, ECON 1014, ECON 1073), or permission of the instructor.

source.section: ECON 3015 The Economics of Strategic Thinking

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Introduction to Development Economics
courses.description: This course introduces students to the models and concepts relevant to understanding major challenges and economic policy analysis in developing and transitional economics. The course examines the similarities and differences of economic issues in developed, developing, and transitional economies.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Canadian Economic Development
courses.description: This course examines the growth and development of the Canadian economy in relation to the endownment with natural resources, changing market conditions, institutions and technology. These concepts are applied to the evolution and role of public policy in Canada and the roots of regionalism in Canada.
courses.prereqText: Some background in Economics, preferably ECON 1013 and ECON 1023.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Intermediate Macroeconomics
courses.description: Macroeconomics seeks to understand the way in which national economies function, and the way they interact with each other at the international level. Key questions are: the determination of a country's standard of living and rate of growth; the causes of recessions, unemployment, and inflation; the determinants of exchange rates and the benefits (or costs) of currency unions; and the determinants of interest rates. This course is an essential building block for higher level study in economics and finance, and is indispensable for understanding stock markets and financial investment.
courses.prereqText: 3 ch of first-year macroeconomics (ECON 1023, or ECON 1024), or ECON 1073.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Public Policy Analysis
courses.description: Introduces public policy analysis from an economic perspective. It covers both microeconomic policy (how and why governments intervene in the marketplace, and the criteria for such intervention)and macroeconomic policy (whether actual stabilization policies are effective). It develops the necessary tools to discuss public policy, and applies them to various sub-fields (such as labour, taxation, government, spending, trade, monopoly, fisheries, etc). The discussion is located in the Canadian context: the assignment of government functions in our Constitution, and fiscal federalism.
courses.prereqText: 3 ch of first-year microeconomics (ECON 1013, or ECON 1014) and 3 ch of first-year macroeconomics (ECON 1023, or ECON 1024), or ECON 1073.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Introduction to Money and Banking
courses.description: Introduces theory of money, history of monetary systems, deposit creation, central and commercial banking, monetary policy and foreign exchange.
courses.prereqText: 3 ch of first-year macroeconomics (ECON 1023, or ECON 1024), or ECON 1073.

source.section: ECON 3103 Introduction to Money and Banking

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Public Finance Analysis
courses.description: Analyzes federal, provincial, and local expenditure and taxation by governments. Both theory and evidence (with an emphasis on Canadian institutions) are emphasized.
courses.prereqText: 3 ch of first-year microeconomics (ECON 1013, or ECON 1014), or ECON 1073.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: The Taxation of Personal Income: Principles and Practice (O)
courses.description: The taxation of personal income in Canada. Topics include the concept of taxable income; capital gains; dividends; deduction vs credits; tax rates; economic efficiency and equity; alternative forms of taxation. This course also examines the Canadian tax treatment of personal income in detail.
courses.prereqText: First-year microeconomics (ECON 1013, or ECON 1014 or ECON 1073), or permission of the instructor.

source.section: ECON 3204 The Taxation of Personal Income: Principles and Practice (O)

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: The Taxation of Business Income: Principles and Practice (O)
courses.description: The taxation of corporate income in Canada. Topics include the structure of the corporate tax system; the concept of integration; typical tax planning strategies. Taxation of partnerships and trusts will be discussed briefly. This course also discusses the Canadian tax system in detail.

source.section: ECON 3205 The Taxation of Business Income: Principles and Practice (O)

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: International Economics: Trade
courses.description: Dive into the theory of international trade. This course covers mercantilism, comparative advantage, and the gains from trade. Explore how factor endowments and industrial organization shape trade patterns and affect income distribution. Examine international capital and labor movements, analyze protectionism, and study the impact of trade agreements on economic development. This knowledge will equip students to analyze global economic policies. NOTE: ECON 3013 recommended.
courses.prereqText: 3 ch of first-year microeconomics (ECON 1001, or ECON 1013, or ECON 1014) and 3 ch of first-year macroeconomics (ECON 1002, or ECON 1023, or ECON 1024), or ECON 1073.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: International Economics: Finance
courses.description: Explore the financing of global trade and capital flows. This course covers the balance of payments, foreign exchange markets, and exchange rates. Examine how macroeconomic policies function under both fixed and flexible exchange rate systems and analyze various international monetary systems. The knowledge gained in this course will provide the tools to understand and analyze international finance and policy. NOTE: ECON 3023 recommended.
courses.prereqText: 3 ch of first-year microeconomics (ECON 1013, or ECON 1014) and 3 ch of first-year macroeconomics (ECON 1023, or ECON 1024), or ECON 1073.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Regional Economic Theory and Policy
courses.description: Concerned with the general theory of regional economic disparities and economic development, and the role of governments (federal and provincial) in alleviating disparities. Emphasizes current problems and policies pertaining to Atlantic Canada.
courses.prereqText: 3 ch of first-year microeconomics (ECON 1013, or ECON 1014), or ECON 1073.

source.section: ECON 3504 Regional Economic Theory and Policy

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Information Technology and the Canadian Economy
courses.description: Blends economic analysis, economic history and public policy to spotlight the role of economics in the context of the revolution in information technology. Topics include: the structural evolution of the Canadian and regional economies, the emergence of knowledge based industries, the economic costs and benefits of education, the demographic and skill composition of Canada's labour force, the economics of technological change and the contemporary role of the information technology, the impact of information technological developments on human rights, the role of the private and public sectors in the new transnational global economy.
courses.prereqText: First-year microeconomics (ECON 1013, or ECON 1014 or ECON 1073), or permission of the instructor.

source.section: ECON 3505 Information Technology and the Canadian Economy

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Business Statistics (Cross-Listed: ADM 2623)
courses.description: Introduces the methods of data presentation and analysis, and their applications to business problems, including measures of data description, probability concepts and distributions, and statistical design theory. Also considers sampling theorem, hypothesis testing using different techniques.
courses.prereqText: 3 ch, MATH 1823, and MATH 1833 or equivalents. Students may not receive credit for both ECON 3601 and ADM 2632.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Management Science (Cross-Listed: ADM 2624)
courses.description: Presents a variety of applications of optimization models to business problems such as allocation, blending, and scheduling. Introduces concepts production planning, inventory control, network models and sequencing.
courses.prereqText: ADM 2623. Students may not receive credit for both ECON 3602 and ADM 2624.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Advanced Statistics for Finance (Cross-Listed: ADM 3628)
courses.description: Examines theory behind statistical techniques such as analysis of variance, simple and multiple regression, non-parametric methods of estimation and hypothesis testing, and time series analysis. Examines the applications of these techniques to problems in finance and other areas of business administration.
courses.prereqText: ADM 2623. Students may not receive credit for both ECON 3628 and ADM 3628.

source.section: ECON 3628 Advanced Statistics for Finance (Cross-Listed: ADM 3628)

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Introduction to Mathematical Economics
courses.description: Learn how to use mathematics in economic analysis. Use techniques for constrained and unconstrained optimization, and apply them to problems of firm and consumer behavior. Learn how to interpret Lagrange multipliers as shadow prices. Apply matrix algebra to study problems of production and allocation in interdependent economies.
courses.prereqText: First-year microeconomics (ECON 1013 or ECON 1014) and first-year macroeconomics (ECON 1023 or ECON 1024), or ECON 1073. In addition, MATH 1843 or MATH 1823, and MATH 1833 or equivalents.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Cost-Benefit Analysis
courses.description: Examine the principles of cost-benefit analysis. This course covers welfare economics, addresses how to treat intangible factors, and considers non-efficiency considerations. Learn about time discounting, various evaluation criteria, and how to account for uncertainty and risk. The knowledge gained in this course will give students the skills to critically evaluate public and private projects. NOTE: ECON 3023 recommended.
courses.prereqText: 3 ch of first-year microeconomics (ECON 1013 or ECON 1014) and 3 ch of first-year macroeconomics (ECON 1023 or ECON 1024), or ECON 1073.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Canada and the New Global Economy
courses.description: This course examines the Canadian economy in the context of the new global economy of the 21st century. Economic theory, economic history and public policy will be the backdrop for a discussion of the trilogy of interactive economic forces that define the new global economy- globalization, trade liberalization and the information technology and communications revolution.
courses.prereqText: First-year microeconomics (ECON 1013, or ECON 1014 or ECON 1073).

source.section: ECON 3705 Canada and the New Global Economy

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Economics of Human Resources
courses.description: How do employers recruit the best employees for the job? How important is money relative to other factors when it comes to hiring and keeping employees? Should good performance on the job be rewarded or should bad performance be penalized? The purpose of this unit is to provide the student with the economic tools of analysis to answer these questions as well as many other important questions in the area of human resource management. Topics include education and training decisions, hiring and turnover, compensation and worker incentives, measuring performance, promotions as a motivator, and team-based production. The analysis of the main issues will be reinforced and complemented with reference to a series of firm-level case studies.
courses.prereqText: 3 ch of first-year microeconomics (ECON 1013, or ECON 1014), or ECON 1073.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Environmental Economics (Cross-listed: ENVS 3755)
courses.description: Explore economic principles for managing environmental resources like air and water. Examine the disparity between optimal and actual resource use in modern economies. Analyze government policies in theory and practice. Learn cost-benefit analysis to evaluate public sector projects using environmental resources. This course develops skills to analyze and address complex environmental economic challenges. NOTE: Credit cannot be counted for both ECON 3755 and ENVS 3755.
courses.prereqText: 3 ch of first-year microeconomics (ECON 1013, or ECON 1014) or ECON 1073, or permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Economics of Climate Change (A) (Cross-listed: ENVS 3766)
courses.description: Climate change is posing a significant challenge to world economies. This course focuses on valuing the consequences of climate change and assessing the costs of mitigation and adaptation. The efficiency of alternative policy instruments such as carbon taxes, tradable emissions permits, voluntary initiatives, and others are assessed. Existing instruments, such as carbon taxes in British Columbia and carbon credit trading on the Chicago Climate Exchange are reviewed and critiqued. The potential contribution of these instruments to the overall achievement of Kyoto Protocol targets set by various countries is examined. NOTE: Credit cannot be counted for both ECON 3766 and ENVS 3766.
courses.prereqText: 3 ch of first-year microeconomics (ECON 1013, or ECON 1014), or ECON 1073, or permission of the instructor.

source.section: ECON 3766 Economics of Climate Change (A) (Cross-listed: ENVS 3766)

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: The Economics of Canadian Immigration
courses.description: An analysis of the role of international migration on the course of Canadian economic development.
courses.prereqText: Both first-year microeconomics (ECON 1013 or ECON 1014) and first-year macroeconomics (ECON 1023 or ECON 1024) or ECON 1073.

source.section: ECON 3775 The Economics of Canadian Immigration

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Introduction to Health Economics
courses.description: The course discusses applications of economic principles and empirical analysis to health and health policy. It considers such matters as the demand for health care, and the supply of health services - both through health practitioners and hospitals; the economic effects of health insurance, health economic evaluation techniques, and public policy formulation. Emphasis is on Canadian health programs and policies.
courses.prereqText: 3 ch of first-year microeconomics (ECON 1013, or ECON 1014), or ECON 1073.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Introduction to Law and Economics
courses.description: This course applies the tools of economic analysis to the study of legal rules and institutions. Topics and case studies in three core areas of the law - property, contracts, and crime and punishment - are used to illustrate and develop two related ideas. The first is that economic principles have guided significant developments in the evolution of the law in many areas, and an understanding of these economic principles will lead to a better understanding of the law as it is currently practiced. The second is that economic analysis can be used to assess and critique current law from a social perspective, leading to improved public policy evaluation and formation in all areas of civil and criminal law.
courses.prereqText: First-year microeconomics (ECON 1013, or ECON 1014 or ECON 1073), or permission of the instructor.

source.section: ECON 3845 Introduction to Law and Economics

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Energy Economics (Cross-listed: ENVS 3865)
courses.description: Applies economic theory to energy issues. Demand for energy and supply of energy are explored in terms of non-renewable and renewable energy resources. Markets for energy resources are discussed. Specific attention is directed to petroleum markets and OPEC behaviour. Public policy issues associated with the energy sector such as the environment and sustainability are addressed. NOTE: Credit cannot be counted for both ECON 3865 and ENVS 3865.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Contemporary Issues in the Canadian Economy
courses.description: Examines a variety of contemporary economic issues, including inflation, unemployment, economic growth, regional disparity, monetary and fiscal policies, the new international economic order, bilateral and multilateral trade agreements.

source.section: ECON 3905 Contemporary Issues in the Canadian Economy

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Advanced Microeconomics
courses.description: Focuses on advanced theory of choice. Topics include choice under uncertainty, the theory of the firm, oligopoly theories, game theory, general equilibrium, and the distribution of income.
courses.prereqText: ECON 3013 and ECON 3665 or an equivalent to ECON 3665.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Advanced Macroeconomics
courses.description: Emphasizes core neo-classical theories as well as Keynesian and post-Keynesian models.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Econometrics I
courses.description: Introduction to basic econometric techniques for estimating and testing economic models. Topics include: review of basic statistics, the nature of econometric models and economic data, regression analysis, hypothesis testing, and applications. Emphasis is on intuition and applications.
courses.prereqText: Any first year economics course and 6 ch Introductory Statistics (e.g. ECON 3601/ADM 2623 and ECON 3628/ADM 3628).

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Mathematical Economics II
courses.description: Apply optimization techniques to economic problems, primarily within a linear framework. The course focuses on using these models to solve practical economic challenges. Students will learn to analyze and interpret solutions, gaining valuable skills in economic modeling and decision-making.
courses.prereqText: ECON 3665, or MATH 2003 and MATH 2013, and ECON 3013.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Introduction to Game Theory (O) (Cross-Listed: MATH 3373)
courses.description: Strategic games, n-person games in normal form, dominated strategies, Nash equilibrium, mixed strategies and mixed strategy equilibrium, games with perfect information, gameswith imperfect information, Bayesian games, extensive games. The course introduces basic non-cooperative game theory and analytical tools for decision makers (consumers,firms, politicians, governments). It is suitable for Mathematics, Economics, Management Science, Political Science, Social Science and Science students or any student with a minor in such disciplines, in particular those in the Mathematics/Statistics-Economics option.
courses.prereqText: MATH 1823 and MATH 1833; or MATH 1003 and MATH 1013; or MATH 1053 and MATH 1063; or ECON 3013; or permission of the instructor.

source.section: ECON 4673 Introduction to Game Theory (O) (Cross-Listed: MATH 3373)

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Topics in Microeconomic Theory
courses.description: Considers the advanced theory of production and consumer demand, expected utility theory, theory of the market, elements of game theory, general equilibrium and welfare.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Topics in Macroeconomics
courses.description: Examines neoclassical, Keynes and Keynesian models, and static, dynamic, equilibrium and disequilibrium models.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Public Policy Research
courses.description: This course provides practical experience in public policy analysis through supervised research. Students will complete research projects assigned by the instructor. These projects are policy-oriented and are chosen in consultation with sponsoring agencies. A formal presentation of the results is required at the end of the course.
courses.prereqText: ECON 3013 and ECON 3023 or permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Regional Economics
courses.description: Examines the history and evolution of the New Brunswick and Atlantic economics applying economic theory and measurement approaches intended to describe the determinants of growth and the process of economic adjustment.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Economic Geography
courses.description: The course explores processes driving spatial patterns of economic activity at the global, national, regional, and local scales. Topic areas include economic globalization, spatial distribution of industrial sectors, multinational corporations, international trade, and regional economic development. The course looks a historical and contemporary skills in upper-income as well as low-and middle-income countries.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: International Money and Finance: Theory and Policy
courses.description: The course covers topics in open economy macroeconomics to help students to become critical reader of popular and ongoing debates about the global economy. Topics include international capital flows; exchange rate regimes; theories of speculative attacks and currency crises; causes and consequences of financial crises; predictions of financial crises; stabilization and adjustment; debt crises; international monetary integration; and scope and functions of international monetary agencies.
courses.prereqText: ECON 3013 and ECON 3023 or equivalent courses.

source.section: ECON 5616 International Money and Finance: Theory and Policy

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Econometrics II
courses.description: Review of matrix algebra. Errors in variables, instrumental variables, simultaneous equations, qualitative and limited dependent variables, dynamic models, model selection criterion, causality, unit roots, single equation cointegration methods. Emphasis is on practical application of simultaneous methods.
courses.prereqText: ECON 4625 or permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Applied Econometrics
courses.description: This course builds on the material covered in ECON 4625, Econometrics I. There are two main objectives to the course: first, to extend the classical model to consider a variety of related topics that are central to data analysis in the social sciences, including discrete and limited dependent variables, lagged dependent variables, panel data, and simultaneous equations; and second, to develop the application of the theory to empirical analysis by considering a variety of real-world examples.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Economics of Human Resources
courses.description: Attention given to the economics of the education process, the theory and implications of innovation, the effects of education and technological change on the distribution of income, and the role of education and technological change in economic growth.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Environmental Economics II
courses.description: Applies economic theory to real-world environmental issues. The theory of environmental externalities is first explored. Then various applications are introduced such as environmental valuation techniques, computable general equilibrium modeling, and environmental accounting procedures. Such environmental issues as deforestation, urban air pollution, and water pollution will be covered.
courses.prereqText: ECON 3755 or permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Transportation Economics I (A)
courses.description: This course focuses on basic tools of economic analysis to determine demand and supply in transportation markets. Considerable attention is devoted to the derivation of market and aggregate demand for transportation services as well as to cost functions as determinants of supply of transportation services. Efficient pricing of transportation services is analysed. Investment criteria are reviewed to determine the efficient pricing. Market failures and imperfections of transportation markets are examined.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Health Economics
courses.description: Discuss and analyse the health economics literature. A set of topics is selected by the instructor for consideration. Selected topics may include demand theory and measurement as applied to health care markets, production and supply theory (in the context of health markets), health economic evaluation methods, managed competition approaches to health care, and public policy analysis. Other topics may be introduced in accordance with the instructor's priorities, or the specific interests of the students.
courses.prereqText: ECON 4013 and ECON 4625 or permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Industrial Organization: Theory
courses.description: Covers welfare economics of competition and monopoly, determinants of industrial structure, theories of industrial pricing, rationalization, technological innovation, and foreign ownership.
courses.prereqText: ECON 3013, with permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Orientation to Educational Studies
courses.description: Teacher candidates will explore essential skills focused on the study of educational scholarship and thinking in higher education. Note: This course will be graded as Credit/No Credit (CR/NCR).

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: BEd in Early Childhood Education Practicum
courses.description: School-based practicum component of the Bachelor of Education in Early Childhood Education involves a six-week term in K-3. Note: This course will be graded as Credit/No Credit (CR/NCR).

source.section: ED 3020 BEd in Early Childhood Education Practicum

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: First Nations Epistemology (Ways of Knowing) (Cross-Listed: INDG 4686)
courses.description: Development of personal and social identity among children in First Nations communities. Implications for classroom practice. Credit cannot be counted for both ED 3022, INDG 4686 or ABRG 3686.

source.section: ED 3022 First Nations Epistemology (Ways of Knowing) (Cross-Listed: INDG 4686)

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Wellbeing and Indigenous Culturally-Grounded Learning
courses.description: Provides experiences for students to acquire knowledge, practice, and tools required to understand, design, intervene in, and promote curriculum and strategies of well-being in educational contexts from Indigenous perspectives. Note: credit cannot be counted for both ED 3021 and ED 3023.

source.section: ED 3023 Wellbeing and Indigenous Culturally-Grounded Learning

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: The Education of Exceptional Learners
courses.description: Provides the student with an introduction to the field of knowledge associated with exceptional learners.

source.section: ED 3031 The Education of Exceptional Learners

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Teaching in a Cultural Context
courses.description: Explores how teachers respond effectively to the culture of children as individuals and to the culture of their people about a variety of cultural contexts, including Canadian Indigenous cultures.

source.section: ED 3033 Teaching in a Cultural Context

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: The Theory and Practice of Education
courses.description: Introduces the dominant theories which influence and shape current thinking and practices in school environments today. Key ideas, their origins, teaching responsibilities, and the components of professional practice are discussed. The course is intended to orient education students to teaching as a profession.

source.section: ED 3041 The Theory and Practice of Education

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: School Law and Organization
courses.description: An overview of the legal, organizational, financial and professional aspects of schools and school systems.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Wabanaki Schools in New Brunswick
courses.description: Schools in Wabanaki communities are governed differently than provincial schools. This course will explore the governance structures of New Brunswick's Wabanaki communities, community schools, and their relationships with Federal and Provincial governments.

source.section: ED 3053 Wabanaki Schools in New Brunswick

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Wabanaki Culture Across the Curriculum
courses.description: Studetns will learn to integrate Wabanaki languages, culture, worldviews, and histories across all school curricular areas through hands-on, place-based learning opportunities with Elders and knowledge keepers.

source.section: ED 3054 Wabanaki Culture Across the Curriculum

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Students, Schools, Equity and Social Justice
courses.description: Explores the social, economic, cultural, and political contexts of learners' lives, discourses of social difference, equity and social justice. Topics include: ableism, sexism, gender bias, racism, class oppression, transphobia, homophobia, and heterosexism, harassment and violence, and the questions these issues raise for schools, curricula and classroom practice.

source.section: ED 3061 Students, Schools, Equity and Social Justice

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Health Promotion in Schools
courses.description: Examines concepts and inter-relationships among nutrition, exercise, and well-being within educational contexts.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Pedagogies of Visual Expression in the Early Years
courses.description: Explores how visual representation supports communication and shared meaning in early learning contexts. Emphasis is placed on creative confidence, interpretive language, and pedagogies that nurture risk-taking, experimentation, and discovery through artistic practices. NOTE: Credit cannot be counted for both ED 3212 and ED 3211.

source.section: ED 3212 Pedagogies of Visual Expression in the Early Years

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Developing Numeracy
courses.description: The study of number relationships and approaches to developing number sense in children and adults. This course will be graded as Credit/No Credit (CR/NCR).

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Developing Geometrical Concepts
courses.description: The study of geometric relationships and approaches to developing spatial sense in children and adults.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Movement Education for the Elementary Teacher
courses.description: Overview of physical education programs in elementary schools. Program planning, practical work.

source.section: ED 3475 Movement Education for the Elementary Teacher

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Health and Physical Education in the Elementary School
courses.description: An overview of curriculum, pedagogy and philosophy of health and physical education for elementary school educators. * Students may receive credit for ED 3478: Health and Physical Education for Elementary Schools or ED 5478: Health and Physical Education in the Elementary School, but not both.

source.section: ED 3478 Health and Physical Education in the Elementary School

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Introduction to Teaching Science in the Early Years
courses.description: Examines science as both a body of knowledge and a way of thinking, with a focus on how young children explore scientific ideas through play, inquiry, and everyday experiences. Note: Credit cannot be counted for ED 3511 and ED 3514.

source.section: ED 3514 Introduction to Teaching Science in the Early Years

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Indigenous Knowledge and Research
courses.description: Provides a comprehensive exploration of Indigenous research methodologies, focusing on culturally relevant and ethically sound approaches to research within Indigenous communities. It emphasizes the importance of understanding Indigenous worldviews, values, and knowledge systems while engaging in the research process.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Netukulimk: Indigenous approach to resource management
courses.description: Explores the concept of Netukulimk, an Indigenous approach to resource management that emphasizes sustainability, respect for nature, and the interconnection of all living things. Students will learn about traditional ecological knowledge and how it intersects with contemporary practices in conservation and environmental stewardship.

source.section: ED 3623 Netukulimk: Indigenous approach to resource management

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Indigenous Dispute Resolution
courses.description: Explores the principles, practices, and frameworks of Indigenous dispute resolution, emphasizing the unique cultural perspectives and traditional methods employed by Indigenous communities. Students will examine various Indigenous approaches to conflict resolution, including restorative justice practices, consensus-building, and community-driven processes.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Information and Communication Technology I
courses.description: Designed to introduce students to basic concepts and practices in the integration of application software within curriculum-based topics. Emphasis is placed on the development of electronic portfolios of technology- enhanced teaching materials for the classroom.

source.section: ED 3862 Information and Communication Technology I

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Introduction to Technology and Skilled Trades Education
courses.description: Examines the development of technology education as a field of study and explores the context in which technology is taught in schools, applied in industry and its impact on society. Current technology applications are examined in areas such as: transportation, construction, communication, manufacturing and biotechnologies.

source.section: ED 3943 Introduction to Technology and Skilled Trades Education

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Practicum for BEd (4 year) Program
courses.description: Eighteen weeks of school and classroom experience. Additional regulations are included in the Education General Regulations under Field Experiences Practicum in Section G of the Calendar. This course will be graded as Credit/No Credit (CR/NCR).
courses.prereqText: Only students who have been officially admitted to the BEd (4 year) program may register for ED 4000. For further information contact the Director of Field Services.

source.section: ED 4000 Practicum for BEd (4 year) Program

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: BEd in Early Childhood Education Practicum I
courses.description: School-based practicum component of the Bachelor of Education in Early Childhood Education involves a three-week term in K-3. NOTE: This course will be graded as Credit/No Credit (CR/NCR)

source.section: ED 4021 BEd in Early Childhood Education Practicum I

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Issues in Training and Development
courses.description: Explores theoretical and practical components of workplace training designed to improve organizational effectiveness and individual performance. Learners examine emergent training topics in a variety of workplace contexts.

source.section: ED 4045 Issues in Training and Development

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Research in Early Childhood Studies
courses.description: Investigates local, national and international research within the field of early childhood. Students will have the opportunity to evaluate research and prepare a research proposal for a project specific to early years.

source.section: ED 4054 Research in Early Childhood Studies

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Advising and Mentoring Adult Learners
courses.description: Examines the characteristics of helping relationships in educational and work settings. Focus will be on the development of skills and strategies conducive to effective advising, coaching and mentoring through collaborative learning, reflection and practice.

source.section: ED 4061 Advising and Mentoring Adult Learners

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Wabanaki BEd Practicum I
courses.description: Introductory practicum including first nine weeks of school and classroom experience. Additional regulations are included in the Educaiton General Regulations under Field Experiences Practicum (Student teaching) in Section G of the calendar. This course will be graded as Credit/No Credit (CR/NCR). Note: Only students who have been officially admitted to the WBEd (4-Year, Elementary) may register for ED 4100. Students are required to remain in good academic standing in their courses and maintain respectful, ethical relationships with colleagues, peers, and instructors in order to enroll in ED 4100 and proceed to their practicum placement.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.description: Students will normally be limited to 6 ch of independent study.
courses.prereqText: Permission of an instructor is required before registration.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Wabanaki BEd Practicum II
courses.description: Advanced practicum including the second nine weeks of school and classroom experience. Additional regulations are included in the Education General Regulations section under Field Experiences Practicum (Student teaching) in Section G of the Calendar. Note: This course will be graded as Credit/No Credit (CR/NCR). Note: Only students who have been officially admitted to the WBEd (4-Year, Elementary) may register for ED 4200. Students are required to remain in good academic standing in their courses and maintain respectful, ethical relationships with colleagues, peers, and instructors in order to enrol in ED 4200 and proceed to their practicum placement.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Multi Modal Literacies in Early Childhood Education
courses.description: Investigate the symbols and tools of digital literacies, play, math, art, music and print.

source.section: ED 4361 Multi Modal Literacies in Early Childhood Education

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Children's Literature, Singing, Poetry and Performance
courses.description: Introduction of the multi-modal world of children's literature through the study of authors, poets and illustrators, and the art of storytelling, singing and poetry performance with young children.

source.section: ED 4363 Children's Literature, Singing, Poetry and Performance

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Health, Equity and Well-Being
courses.description: In this course, we will unpack complex understandings of what it means for educators to embrace equitable practices in the interests of of children's health, well-being, and belonging. Course topics include diverse abilities, mental and physical health , social responsibility, and self-care. We will explore socially inclusive and culturally sensitive learning environments and how democratic and sustainable practices are nurtured.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Treaty Education
courses.description: Providing students with knowledge of the Indigenous understanding of the treaties signed between Indigenous peoples and the British and Canadian governments between the 18th and 20th centuries and the Peace and Friendship Treaties signed in the Maritimes in the 18th century, specifically. It will also help students think about how to convey the history of treaty-making and the competing understandings of the treaties and that promotes reconciliation.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Teaching First Nations Learner
courses.description: Teaching methods, learning strategies, program planning, with emphasis on a particular learning level.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Teaching First Nations Children's Literature
courses.description: Examines the philosophy and process of teaching First Nations Literature in an integrated curriculum for primary and elementary children. Includes practical classroom experience.

source.section: ED 4688 Teaching First Nations Children's Literature

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Information and Communication Technology II
courses.description: An advanced course in the integration of ICT in the classroom. Students should have previously taken ED 3862 or be able to demonstrate sufficient background knowledge in application software. Focus will also include emerging trends in educational technologies.

source.section: ED 4862 Information and Communication Technology II

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Teaching and Learning Theories I
courses.description: An introduction to teaching as a reflective, professional practice focused upon three themes: Learning and Learners; Establishing a Classroom Context to Support Learning; and Professional Concerns for Teachers. Field experience is central to the course with students expected to apply course ideas in the classroom and reflect on that experience in seminars. This course will be graded as Credit/No Credit (CR/NCR).

source.section: ED 5001 Teaching and Learning Theories I

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Teaching and Learning Theories II
courses.description: A continuation of the examination of teaching as a reflective, professional practice focused upon three themes: Learning and Learners; Establishing a Classroom Context to Support Learning; and Professional Concerns for Teachers. Field experience is central to the course with students expected to apply course ideas in the classroom and reflect on that experience in seminars. This course will be graded as Credit/No Credit (CR/NCR).

source.section: ED 5002 Teaching and Learning Theories II

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Teaching and Learning Theories III
courses.description: As a culmination of Teaching and Learning Theory I and II, this course will facilitate students integrating their personal backgrounds, academic and professional education through the development of a significant project. Projects will be shared with peers as well as the broader professional and public community in a senior conference. This course will be graded as Credit/No Credit (CR/NCR).

source.section: ED 5003 Teaching and Learning Theories III

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Preparing for Prior Learning Assessment
courses.description: Through the use of reflection, self-assessment and personal journals, participants will create an experience-based dossier which will describe their personal philosophy, current professional practices, and needs for further learning.

source.section: ED 5011 Preparing for Prior Learning Assessment

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Special Topics in Education
courses.description: In consultation with faculty advisor. (Intended for students in the DAUS.)

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Transformative Learning
courses.description: Explores new concepts for working with adult learners. Investigates critical thinking, critical self-reflection and transformative learning.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Educational Psychology
courses.description: This course is designed to survey selected principles, issues and research in educational psychology. A number of learner, teacher and contextual variables will be addressed.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Inclusion from Early Years
courses.description: An examination of personal, societal and school assumptions about the meaning and importance of inclusion in life and learning from childhood. Inclusive models of education will be examined.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Special Topics in Education
courses.description: In consultation with faculty advisor. (Intended for students in the DAUS.)

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Indigenous Education
courses.description: Explores traditional First Nations pedagogy and concepts of education in comparison with those which have shaped formal schooling. It will further describe roles and responsibilities of schools, teachers, and communities in educating First Nations students. Notes: This course will be graded as Credit/No Credit (CR/NCR). Credit cannot be counted for both ED 3043 and ED 5043.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Inclusive Design
courses.description: Enhances teacher candidates' knowledge of diverse student learning needs and dynamic inclusive practices for enhancing the learning environment for all learners. This course will be graded as Credit/No Credit (CR/NCR)

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Special Topics in Education
courses.description: In consultation with faculty advisor. (Intended for students in the DAUS.)

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Educating At-Risk Students
courses.description: Characteristics of the at-risk student. Psychological, social, and economic effects of dropping out. Remedial strategies involving learning, teaching, counselling, school climate, and school organization. Exemplary programs for at-risk students and for dropout prevention.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Practicum
courses.description: School-based experience component of the 10-month B.Ed. involves an observation practicum during K-12 students' first week of classes in September, a seven-week Intermediate Practicum in the fall term, and en eight-week Advanced Practicm during the winter term. This course will be graded as Credit/No Credit (CR/NCR). NOTE: Students are required to be in good acadeimc standing and maintain respectful, ethical relationships with colleagues, peers, and instructors to proceed to their practicum placement and remain enrolled in ED 5050.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Wabanaki Perspectives in Creating Holistic Classroom Environments
courses.description: Examines complex dynamics of classroom environments through holistic, Wabanaki perspectives and explores effective strategies focused on creating nurturing, inclusive, culturally responsive classroom communities. Emphasis will be on trauma-invested practices, Wabanaki perspectives, and strengths-based principles.

source.section: ED 5055 Wabanaki Perspectives in Creating Holistic Classroom Environments

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Cultural Constructions of Childhood
courses.description: A historical examination of cultural constructions of childhood and family and the implications of these various constructions upon the education of young children.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Personal Growth and Helping
courses.description: Focus on understanding human development; particularly the development of the self and how such development may be nurtured or thwarted within the educational setting. Students will examine issues such as identity, personality, self-awareness, relationships, and basic counselling skills. These issues will be regarded on two levels: as aspects of the individual self and as aspects of the learning environment.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Comprehensive Sex Education Methods
courses.description: Students will explore research-informed best practices in comprehensive sex education in early childhood, primary, middle and secondary school contexts. Students will critically engage with research-informed strategies, pedagogies, and approaches to support school-based comprehensive sex education for young people in New Brunswick.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Education in International Contexts
courses.description: Examines the nature of education in a range of international contexts with a particular focus on understanding how culture and world view shape education and comparing and contrasting trends and issues for teachers and the teaching in those contexts. It is designed to provide teacher education students with a global perspective on the education profession.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Cultural Contexts of Education
courses.description: Examines history, philosophy, and social contexts of education. Through each of these disciplines, teacher candidates explore broad concerns and impacts of ethics and equity with connections to curriculum, pedagogy, and school practice. Notes: This course will be graded as Credit/No Credit CR/NCR. Credit cannot be counted for both ED 5070 and ED 5072,

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: History of Education
courses.description: Explores current problems within education as well as aims, curriculum, teaching, administration and ideas viewed from a historical perspective.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Learning Disabilities: Introduction
courses.description: Concepts, definitions and terminology. A preventive approach.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Behavioural/Emotional Disorders
courses.description: An overview of various emotional and behavioural disorders of children and young people and the ways in which coping and management strategies can be applied to develop self-discipline and control.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Differentiating Instruction in the Classroom
courses.description: Allows teachers to explore current research on differentiation; familiarize themselves with many strategies for differentiating content, process and product; develop differentiation lesson plans including pre-assessment strategies as well as classroom management strategies intended for classroom application.

source.section: ED 5097 Differentiating Instruction in the Classroom

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Practicum
courses.description: Fifteen weeks of school and classroom experience. This cours will be graded as Credit/No Credit (CR/NCR).
courses.prereqText: Only students admitted to the BEd (4-year) program in Montreal may register.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Curriculum and Evaluation in the Early Years
courses.description: Examines characteristics of early years learners and the role of the teacher as observer and curriculum developer in theory and practice.

source.section: ED 5102 Curriculum and Evaluation in the Early Years

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Project Approach in the Early Years
courses.description: Planning a multi-disciplinary curriculum approach building on children's curiosities, enabling them to interact, question, connect, problem solve, communicate and represent learning, focusing on the teacher's role in implementing a project-based approach in the early years.

source.section: ED 5103 Project Approach in the Early Years

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Observation and Pedagological Documentation
courses.description: Investigates current practices in observing and documenting children's learning in early childhood environments in collaboration with learners, colleagues and families.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Connecting Home and Schooled Literacies
courses.description: Examines theory and practice of connecting home and school literacies for the development of a literate community.

source.section: ED 5105 Connecting Home and Schooled Literacies

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Digital Literacies in the Early Years
courses.description: Investigates the impact of technologies on play and emergent digital literacies, exploring ways in which educators and families can support engagement with technologies (or digital envrionments) in early childhood settings and homes.

source.section: ED 5106 Digital Literacies in the Early Years

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Orientation to Counselling
courses.description: Introduction to the role of the counsellor in various settings, including the public education system. Students will examine the counsellor as a person, roles of the client and counsellor, the counselling process, counselling skills, counselling theories, and counselling in the individual and group context.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Career Guidance
courses.description: Introduction to understanding the importance of and the application of career development throughout the public education system. Topics include the historical development of career guidance, theories of vocational development, career education in the curriculum, career assessments, Social Emotional Learning, Global Competencies, Problem Based Learning, Experiential Learning, Labour Market information, Universal Design for Learning, and working with students from various minority groups.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Creativity, Images and Meaning (Cross-Listed: FNAT 3703)
courses.description: Addresses the significance of creativity in image-making, communication, and self-expression. Imagery as a primary form of communication provides a basis for exploring a wide variety of topics, ideas and issues. Analyzing images, exploring different visual media, and communicating through visual means are key components of this course. Connections that exist between images and other forms of communication and self-expression are also explored.

source.section: ED 5154 Creativity, Images and Meaning (Cross-Listed: FNAT 3703)

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Integrated Curriculum for the First Nations Learner
courses.description: Culture-based education: design, development, and implementation. Appropriate evaluation and assessment.

source.section: ED 5162 Integrated Curriculum for the First Nations Learner

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Cultural Studies and Critical Pedagogy
courses.description: The study of the entire range of a society's arts, beliefs, institutions, and communicative practices and its application to education.

source.section: ED 5166 Cultural Studies and Critical Pedagogy

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Interpreting Play for Curriculum Development
courses.description: An exploration of the literature on play including play as reflective pedagogy. A variety of theoretical perspectives will be brought to the interpretation of children's play. The teacher's role in creating physical and social environments that facilitate cognitive, emotional, social, spiritual, and physical growth will be examined.

source.section: ED 5167 Interpreting Play for Curriculum Development

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Assessment in Education
courses.description: This course will deal with the what, why and how of classroom-based assessment. It will examine exemplary practices related to formative assessment (assessment for and as learning), as well as summative assessment (assessment of learning). The course will also examine the nature and purpose of large-scale assessment within education. Topics will include defining clear learning/assessment targets and standards-based assessment, designing assessment techniques, matching assessment with learning and communicating assessment results.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Introduction to Standardized Testing Instruments
courses.description: An examination of selected standardized tests used in the public school system.

source.section: ED 5174 Introduction to Standardized Testing Instruments

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Classroom Assessment
courses.description: An examination of current assessment issues, procedures, and techniques and how these can be used to improve teaching and student learning.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Feminist Theory and Education
courses.description: Explores how feminist theories have re-thought educational practice, with specific focus on issues of knowledge, curriculum, classroom pedagogy, research, and educational policy.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Problem Solving with Young Children
courses.description: Examines research and theory of problem-solving with young children. Emphasizes the teacher's role as the facilitator of problem-solving across the curriculum.

source.section: ED 5182 Problem Solving with Young Children

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Independent Studies
courses.description: Students will normally be limited to 6 ch of independent study. NOTE: Permission of an instructor is required before registration.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Creativity and Visual Arts in Teaching and Learning
courses.description: Addresses the importance of creativity and innovation in education, explores applications in teaching, and builds creative capacity through visual and other modes of communication. It is a dynamic, interactive and cross-disciplinary course designed to increase creative, critical and divergent thinking, and art making skills in order to enhance meaning making, problem solving and self-expression.Students will also learn to design creative and innovative teaching strategies relevant and applicable to teaching visual art and related subject areas.

source.section: ED 5209 Creativity and Visual Arts in Teaching and Learning

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Integrated Learning Through Art
courses.description: Art education theories and practices as they apply to learning across the curriculum.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Issues in Art Education
courses.description: Examines contemporary issues in Art Education with a practical focus on developing teaching strategies that address local, national, and international issues being debated in art education.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Music for the Classroom Teacher
courses.description: Examines appropriate methodology, skills and content for the elementary classroom teacher to use in teaching music in a variety of settings. Students will sing, play an instrument, listen and move to music.

source.section: ED 5242 Music for the Classroom Teacher

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Music in the Elementary School
courses.description: Study of methods and materials current in the elementary school. Development of skills and curriculum. Study of the young learner and music.
courses.prereqText: 9 ch in music courses or permission of the instructor.

source.section: ED 5243 Music in the Elementary School

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Literacy
courses.description: Addresses the theoretical underpinnings and implementation methods of the six strands in the teaching of literacy: reading, writing, listening, speaking, viewing and visual representation.

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Drama Across the Curriculum (Middle, Secondary)
courses.description: Group process drama will be employed to study in any curriculum subject, such as history, mathematics, science and social studies. No experience necessary.

source.section: ED 5314 Drama Across the Curriculum (Middle, Secondary)

courses.subject: ED
courses.title: Dramatization of Literature (Elementary, Middle)
